Link 4 as guessed is false both ways, by October's own theorems: a rising order re-optimizing keeps a condition for ever exactly where its draw is within the renewal; an order nearing a set point drains like a rising one below it, has a draining optimum at it, and ends a condition by joint excess. Holding is decided by draw against renewal; the order's shape decides only how much is drawn. Link 5 is a renaming. Link 6 is apart: the formed goal lives on a finite periphery construction, and the set level is handed in throughout Regulation and SetPointOptimum.

what_the_modules_say.in_plain_words: An order nears a set point s where it ranks above every outcome between s and the other, strictly nearer somewhere; any order falling with distance is one. Where an eligible outcome reaches s, every optimum stands at s; of what lies beyond the class says nothing. Below s it takes the whole capacity beyond, as a rising order does. At s, in a balanced step where the whole gains nothing, the beyond falls by exactly the loss. Holders losing together more than a condition is given end it.

what_the_modules_say.in_plain_words: An order rises where it ranks above every outcome higher on what couples in. With room every optimum stands at the least level beyond; in an exchange each member takes its whole capacity there. Over re-optimizing steps that is one draw k each step, so a need is kept for ever exactly where k ≤ the renewal r.

Main theorem: nothing restricts significance exactly where, at each standpoint, 'all within my boundary has significance' holds under some drawing and under every drawing alike; that invariance carries the whole content.
